key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: The framework can lower electricity costs and improve operational control for buildings with PV, batteries, heat pumps, and dynamic tariffs.
method: Train on-policy and off-policy DRL agents on an expanded state space with demand, PV, battery SoC, prices, weather, and calendar features.
Compare A2C and PPO against off-policy methods for cumulative reward and policy stability.
Apply post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned control policies and decision behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, with A2C and PPO performing best on cumulative reward and stability.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on forecast quality and real-world deployment conditions, so explainability does not eliminate the need for careful validation and safety constraints.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
